newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan plans to cut drug prices next spring -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan plans to cut drug prices next spring -- paper.

text.p: Japan's Health Ministry plans to lower the price of drugs provided by hospitals to patients in the spring and the move is seen having a negative impact on the earnings of pharmaceutical and drug-related companies, a Japanese newspaper said on Wednesday.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun economic daily said industry sources think the price cut could be as large as five percent from current levels.
The government reimburses hospitals for drugs they dispense under the National Health Insurance system so it has a hand in setting prices.
The ministry has already cut drug prices this year and if it cuts prices further next year, it would be unusual as it usually reviews drug prices every other year, the paper said.
But a planned increase in the consumption tax by two percent is likely to spur the move, the paper said.
The ministry was not immediately available for comment.
